messages.subject: Q on pcount()
parts:
Dear all,

I am fitting a large number of binomial mixture models to 2015 data from my favourite monitoring program, the MHB. Things work fine, but I just got worried by the following info at the end of the summary of the model fits:

AIC: 356.3208
Number of sites: 266
Sites removed: 186
......

In 2015, one out of the 267 quadrats were not surveyed, so 266 sites makes sense. But what does the "186 sites removed" mean ? That does not make sense to me; I have 47 sites with the third of 3 surveys missing, and two obsCovs (survey date and duration) similarly have 47 missing data for the third survey. But I don't see how any site would have been removed.

Thanks for enlightenment,

best regards  --  Marc

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Q on pcount()
parts:
hi Marc (and all)
,
 In Marc's example,

AIC: 356.3208
Number of sites: 266
Sites removed: 186
......

the note "Sites removed: 186" is literally just noting that a single site, site number 186, has been removed from the data set.  This site is removed because it had 3 missing values in one of the covariates and so the observed counts couldn't be used to fit the model.
 If you set the data to NA for some other site, say site number 100, then the message will read:

 Sites removed: 100 186

etc..
 So this is not a problem, as it turns out.
regards
andny
